'''Óscar Sonejee Masand''' (born 26 March 1976) is an Andorran former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

He began his club career as a youth player with [[UE Sant Julià|Sant Julià]] before playing for several teams based in Andorra, including three spells with [[FC Andorra]] and three with [[FC Lusitanos|Lusitanos]]. He also spent four years with [[FC Santa Coloma]], helping the side win two [[Primera Divisió]] titles. He retired from playing at the age of 40 in January 2017 during his third spell with Lusitanos.

He made his international debut for [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] in 1997 during a defeat to [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]]. He scored the goal in 2000 that secured the nation's first ever point in a competitive international fixture when they drew 1–1 with [[Malta national football team|Malta]]. He went on to become his country's most [[Cap (sport)|capped]] international player until 2015 when his record was surpassed by [[Ildefons Lima]] and he was the first Andorran player to reach 100 international caps. He finished his career with [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|106 caps]] and four goals for the Andorra national team, placing him second to Ildefons Lima in both categories.<ref name="EU Football">{{cite web |url=http://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=19717 |title=Óscar Sonejee |work=EU Football |access-date=28 September 2014 |archive-date=15 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201015121740/https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=19717 |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 2016 and 2017, he managed the [[Andorra national under-17 football team|Andorra under-17 side]].

==Early life==
Sonejee was born on 26 March 1976 in [[Santa Coloma d'Andorra|Santa Coloma]], Andorra.<ref name="Soccerway"/> His parents were both Indian but had decided to emigrate from their home in [[Delhi]] in the 1970s with their first two sons before Sonejee was born.<ref name="gain">{{cite web |url=https://m.sportskeeda.com/football/oscar-sonejee-a-champions-league-footballer-who-was-indias-loss-and-andorra-gain |title=Oscar Sonejee: A Champions League footballer, who was India's loss and Andorra's gain |website=sportskeeda.com |last=Basu |first=Suromitro |date=21 October 2016 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427232757/https://www.sportskeeda.com/indian-football/oscar-sonejee-a-champions-league-footballer-who-was-indias-loss-and-andorra-gain |archive-date=27 April 2023 }}</ref><ref name="el">{{cite web |url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/futbol/2015-06-29/oscar-sonejee-cumplio-su-sueno-de-bollywood-con-la-seleccion-de-andorra_905044/ |title=Óscar Sonejee cumplió su sueño de Bollywood con la selección de Andorra |publisher=El Confidencial |last=Ruiz |first=David |language=Spanish |date=29 June 2015 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001182053/https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/futbol/2015-06-29/oscar-sonejee-cumplio-su-sueno-de-bollywood-con-la-seleccion-de-andorra_905044/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After living in [[Paris]], his father moved to [[Barcelona]] where he spent a year. However, he quickly looked to move on after believing the city was too suited to tourists and instead moved to Andorra, a small principality in the [[Pyrenees]] mountains, on the recommendation of other local Hindu merchants. After settling in the country, his wife and two sons moved to live with him and the family remained there once it gained independence in March 1993.<ref name="gain"/><ref name="el"/> Sonejee was born soon after, being the only member of the family born outside India.<ref name="el"/>

Sonejee's first sporting participation was in winter sports, traditionally more popular in the mountainous region. However, in sixth grade, he played [[Association football|football]] for the first time and quickly took up the game. He speaks fluent Catalan and Hindi and can speak some English.<ref name="gain"/>

==Club career==
Sonejee began his career as a youth player with his local side [[UE Sant Julià|Sant Julià]]. His early performances for Andorra at youth level led to him being offered a trial with [[La Liga]] side [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] after being spotted by one of the club's scouts. However, the trial was ultimately unsuccessful.<ref name="gain"/> He instead joined [[FC Andorra]], an Andorran team that competes in the [[Spanish football league system]]. He featured eleven times for the club in the [[Segunda División B]] during the [[1997–98 Segunda División B|1997–98 season]] as they suffered relegation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/j/j302111.html |title=Óscar: Óscar Sonejee Masand |website=bdfutbol.com |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001182253/https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/j/j302111.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2008, Sonejee was approached over a potential move to his parents' homeland India, receiving offers from [[East Bengal F.C.|East Bengal]] and [[Churchill Brothers S.C.|Churchill Brothers]]. He originally signed a deal with East Bengal but later decided to accept the offer from Goa-based Churchill Brothers as he believed the culture in the city was more European based and would be easier to acclimatise to and the club was closer to the home of his wife's parents.<ref name="toi">{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/Sonejee-Masand-set-to-join-Churchill-Brothers/articleshow/5091754.cms |title=Sonejee Masand set to join Churchill Brothers |work=The Times of India|last=Mergulhao |first=Marcus |date=6 October 2009 |access-date=1 October 2018}}</ref> However, he later discovered that his original contract with East Bengal was still valid and both clubs claimed ownership. When Churchill attempted to register Sonejee, the [[All India Football Federation]] (AIFF) blocked the move as they had already received a registration request by East Bengal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/1064/i-league/2009/10/11/1553798/i-league-your-itc-request-for-sonejee-cant-be-processed-aiff |title=I-League: Your ITC Request For Sonejee Can't Be Processed – AIFF To Churchill Brothers |website=goal.com |last=Bali |first=Rahul |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001220553/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/1064/i-league/2009/10/11/1553798/i-league-your-itc-request-for-sonejee-cant-be-processed-aiff |url-status=live }}</ref> The situation eventually led to Sonejee backing out of a move to India, having spent a month training with Churchill,<ref name="el"/> and instead signing for [[FC Santa Coloma|Santa Coloma]] in his home nation.<ref name="gain"/>

The most successful period of his career came during a four-year spell with Santa Coloma between 2008 and 2012 where he helped the side to win back-to-back [[Primera Divisió]] titles during the [[2009–10 Primera Divisió|2009–10]] and [[2010–11 Primera Divisió|2010–11 seasons]]. He also won two [[Copa Constitució]] titles in [[2009 Copa Constitució|2009]] and [[2012 Copa Constitució|2012]].<ref name="Soccerway"/>

After returning to his first team Sant Julià in 2015, Sonejee undertook his coaching badges alongside his playing career, obtaining a UEFA [[UEFA A Licence|A]] and [[UEFA B Licence|B Licence]].<ref name="gain"/> He returned to [[FC Lusitanos|Lusitanos]] the following year after being convinced by coach Raul Canete to postpone his retirement for another season.<ref name="incom">{{cite web |url=https://www.bondia.ad/esports/oscar-sonejee-lincombustible |title=Òscar Sonejee, l'incombustible |publisher=Bondia |last=Duaso |first=Victor |language=Catalan |date=26 August 2016 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=21 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021211751/http://www.bondia.ad/esports/oscar-sonejee-lincombustible |url-status=live }}</ref> However, in January 2017, he officially announced his retirement from playing at the age of 40.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/internacional/20170117/413447506816/andorra-retira-oscar-sonejee.html |title=Óscar Sonejee anuncia su retirada |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |last=Aguilar |first=Àxel |language=Spanish |date=17 January 2017 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001142442/https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/internacional/20170117/413447506816/andorra-retira-oscar-sonejee.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Óscar Sonejee.jpg|thumb|upright|Sonejee playing for Andorra in 2009]]
Sonejee began his career at the same time as Andorra declared independence and formed its own footballing governing body, the [[Andorran Football Federation]] (AFF) in 1994. As such, he was present in his nation's youth sides as they began competing in international matches.<ref name="gain"/> He made his international debut in 1997 in a 4–1 [[Exhibition match|friendly]] loss to [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]] at the [[Kuressaare linnastaadion]] in Andorra's second international fixture following their independence. In his second game three days later, he scored his first goal, in a defeat by the same margin to [[Latvia national football team|Latvia]] at the [[Daugava Stadium (Riga)|Daugava Stadium]] in [[Riga]]. He captained the team for the first time on 12 October 2005 against [[Armenia national football team|Armenia]], scoring an [[own goal]] in a 0–3 home defeat in [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification]].<ref name="EU Football"/>

Despite making his debut, Sonejee was still eligible to represent his parents' country [[India national football team|India]] as he did not possess an Andorran passport at the time. He later admitted that, had he received a call up, he would have switched allegiance to India but stated "since I saw nobody was interested, I decided to continue playing for Andorra, and obtained that passport."<ref name="gain"/> In February 2000, he scored for Andorra, helping the side gain their first ever point in an international fixture by drawing 1–1 with [[Malta national football team|Malta]] in the [[2000 Rothmans International Tournament]].<ref name="gain"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ando-intres.html |title=Andorra – List of International Matches |publisher=The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation |last=Di Maggio |first=Roberto |access-date=6 October 2018 |archive-date=29 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629022537/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ando-intres.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 March 2007, during a [[UEFA Euro 2008]] [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|qualifier]], he was involved in a spat with England striker [[Wayne Rooney]], resulting with both players being booked and Rooney was substituted soon after by England manager [[Fabio Capello]] for fear of being sent off.<ref name="toi"/> Sonejee later accused Rooney of being arrogant and insulting him during the match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/2685097/Fabio-Capello-urges-England-to-keep-their-World-Cup-cool-in-Andorra-Football.html |title=Fabio Capello urges England to keep their World Cup cool in Andorra |newspaper=The Telegraph |last=Winter |first=Henry |date=5 September 2008 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001182631/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/2685097/Fabio-Capello-urges-England-to-keep-their-World-Cup-cool-in-Andorra-Football.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 6 June 2015, Sonejee became the first Andorran to earn [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|100 caps]], when he captained the side to a 1–0 friendly home defeat to [[Equatorial Guinea national football team|Equatorial Guinea]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Duaso|first1=Victor|title=Òscar Sonejee, el primer centenari|trans-title=Óscar Sonejee, the first centurion|url=http://www.bondia.ad/esports/oscar-sonejee-el-primer-centenari|access-date=8 June 2015|publisher=Bon Dia|date=7 June 2015|language=Catalan|archive-date=1 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901045904/https://www.bondia.ad/esports/oscar-sonejee-el-primer-centenari|url-status=live}}</ref> Prior to kick-off, he was presented with an honorary cap and medal by [[Victor Santos (football official)|Victor Santos]], the president of the AFF.<ref name="el"/>

Sonejee retired from international football on 12 November 2015, with his final game for Andorra coming in a 1–0 friendly home defeat to [[Saint Kitts and Nevis national football team|Saint Kitts and Nevis]]; his national record of 106 caps was surpassed by [[Ildefons Lima]] in August 2017.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ildefons Lima: l'home rècord |trans-title=Ildefons Lima: the record man |url=https://www.elperiodic.ad/noticia/59552/lhome-record |access-date=31 August 2018 |work=El Periòdic |date=17 August 2017 |language=Catalan |archive-date=1 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901003743/https://www.elperiodic.ad/noticia/59552/lhome-record |url-status=live }}</ref> At the time of his last cap, he was also Andorra's oldest ever international player at 39 years and 230 days. However, his record was surpassed in 2018 by [[Juli Sánchez]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/andorra/tab/stats/option/oldest/ |title=Andorra national football team statistics and records: oldest players |website=11v11.com |publisher=AFS Enterprises |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001220601/https://www.11v11.com/teams/andorra/tab/stats/option/oldest/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Managerial career==
Sonejee managed the Andorra under-16 team at two UEFA youth tournaments, in Luxembourg in 2014 and Montenegro in 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://m.andorradifusio.ad/esports/seleccio-sub-16-prepara-lestrena-europa |title=La selecció sub-16 prepara l'estrena a Europa |publisher=Andorra Difusio |language=Catalan |date=11 April 2014 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001182918/http://m.andorradifusio.ad/esports/seleccio-sub-16-prepara-lestrena-europa |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://m.andorradifusio.ad/esports/sub-16-vol-repetir-gesta-contra-luxemburg |title=La sub-16 vol repetir gesta contra Luxemburg |publisher=Andorra Difusio |language=Catalan |date=14 April 2015 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=1 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001185258/http://m.andorradifusio.ad/esports/sub-16-vol-repetir-gesta-contra-luxemburg |url-status=live }}</ref> He was appointed as manager of the [[Andorra national under-17 football team|Andorra under-17 side]] in January 2016, remaining in charge until October 2017.<ref name="Soccerway"/>

==Personal life==
Sonejee is of Indian heritage and works as an [[insurance]] salesman.<ref name="gain"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/captain-insurance-salesman-everything-you-7735125 |title=Their captain is an insurance salesman... Everything you need to know about Andorra ahead of Euro 2016 qualifier with Wales |publisher=WalesOnline |last=Bywater |first=Alex |date=8 September 2014 |access-date=1 October 2018 |archive-date=2 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002020044/https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/captain-insurance-salesman-everything-you-7735125 |url-status=live }}</ref> His wife is also from India, hailing from [[Bandra]],<ref name="gain"/> and the pair married in [[Jaipur]].<ref name="el"/> They have two children together.<ref name="incom"/> He is a fan of [[Bollywood]] cinema.<ref name="el"/>
